facts.content: Patient reports right knee pain and clicking during runs, along with intermittent tingling in the toes.
facts.source_text: CC: R knee pain + clicking with runs; intermittent toe tingling

facts.content: Onset of symptoms was approximately 2 weeks ago.
facts.source_text: Onset: ~2 wks

facts.content: Symptoms are in the context of marathon training that started approximately 1 month ago with runs ranging 4–8 miles.
facts.source_text: Context: Marathon training (started ~1 mo; runs 4–8 mi)

facts.content: Patient experiences pain starting around 20 minutes into a run, worsening, and causing them to stop their last run early.
facts.source_text: Pain pattern: Starts ~20 min into run (~2.5–3 mi); worsening; stopped last run early

facts.content: There is a clicking especially during flexion to extension during abdominal workouts.
facts.source_text: Mechanical sx: Clicking esp. with flex→extend during ab workouts

facts.content: Pain is located centrally in the right knee, slightly lateral.
facts.source_text: Location: Central R knee, slightly lateral

facts.content: Initial mild swelling after the first run resolved with ice, and there is none currently.
facts.source_text: Swelling: Mild after first run → resolved with ice; none currently

facts.content: Patient can fully flex and extend the knee with no locking or giving way; stairs and walking are okay.
facts.source_text: Function: Full flex/extend; no locking/giving way; stairs/walking ok

facts.content: There was one episode of right toe tingling post-run that resolved.
facts.source_text: Neurovasc: 1 episode R toe tingling post-run (resolved)

facts.content: Patient has a history of hyperopia.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: Hyperopia

facts.content: Patient has undergone LASIK surgery.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: LASIK

facts.content: Patient had a prior severe urinary tract infection requiring emergency room evaluation to rule out kidney stones.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: prior severe UTI (ER, r/o kidney stones)

facts.content: Patient had a remote ice-hockey fall resulting in a large bruise.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: remote ice-hockey fall with large bruise

facts.content: Patient takes Ibuprofen as needed, up to 400 mg.
facts.source_text: Meds/OTC: Ibuprofen PRN (≤400 mg)

facts.content: Patient takes Aleve as needed.
facts.source_text: Meds/OTC: Aleve PRN

facts.content: Patient takes vitamin D.
facts.source_text: Meds/OTC: vitamin D

facts.content: Patient takes melatonin.
facts.source_text: Meds/OTC: melatonin

facts.content: Patient takes Xanax as needed for sleep.
facts.source_text: Meds/OTC: Xanax PRN for sleep

facts.content: Patient is very active and currently training for a marathon.
facts.source_text: SH: Very active; marathon trainee

facts.content: Patient occasionally smokes cannabis in the form of a joint.
facts.source_text: SH: occasional cannabis (smokes a joint)

facts.content: Right knee pain with activity and intermittent clicking for approximately 2 weeks in the context of marathon training; no instability or locking; transient swelling; one transient right toe paresthesia.
facts.source_text: Assessment: 1) R knee pain with activity and intermittent clicking x ~2 wks in context of marathon training; no instability/locking; transient swelling; one transient R toe paresthesia

facts.content: Advised relative rest and to reduce or hold running; patient should not run through pain.
facts.source_text: Activity: Relative rest; reduce/hold runs; do not run through pain

facts.content: Continue regular icing.
facts.source_text: Ice: Continue regular icing

facts.content: Start a stronger NSAID instead of Ibuprofen; take it with food and do not take concurrently with Ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: Meds: Start stronger NSAID instead of ibuprofen; take with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen

facts.content: Referral to physiotherapy for a comprehensive knee assessment has been placed.
facts.source_text: Referral: Physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment (referral placed)

facts.content: Consider imaging based on physio assessment or if symptoms persist to assess cartilage.
facts.source_text: Imaging: Consider based on physio assessment/persistent sx to assess cartilage

facts.content: Safety net for urgent review if persistent swelling, heat or redness, fever, feeling unwell, or if the knee locks or cannot bend or straighten.
facts.source_text: Safety net: Urgent review if persistent swelling, heat/redness, fever/unwell, or if knee locks/cannot bend/straighten

facts.content: Follow-up for in-person exam if physiotherapy wait is long.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If physio wait is long, book clinic visit for in-person exam
